title: Best Quattr Alternatives (2026): Six Options by Need
metaTitle: Best Quattr Alternatives (2026): Six Options by Need
metaDescription: Six Quattr alternatives with public prices checked 3 Oct 2026: AEOeye ($0 or $29 once), Otterly, Peec AI, Nightwatch, AthenaHQ and Profound.
shortAnswer: The best Quattr alternative depends on why you are leaving. For a one-off snapshot, AEOeye is free for a ChatGPT check and $29 once for five engines. For daily tracking at a public price, Otterly starts at $29 a month, Peec AI at $95 and Nightwatch at €99. Profound, like Quattr, ends in a sales call. This guide rests on public documentation as of 3 October 2026; we have not tested any of these products hands-on.
intro:
AEOeye is one of the options below, so treat our placement with that in mind; we say where it is weaker. Quattr's facts come from its own public pages, and so does each alternative's price, read on 3 October 2026.

Older lists, including the earlier version of this page, show Profound at $99 a month and Nightwatch at about $32 plus a $99 AI add-on. Neither appears on those vendors' current pricing pages, so both are gone here.

sections.heading: Why look for a Quattr alternative?
sections.body:
Most searches for an alternative trace back to three things Quattr's own pages state: no public price, a platform sized for a team that runs a program, and a trial route that depends on your use case. None makes it a bad tool; each makes it a poor fit for some buyers.

- **No price to plan against.** Its [pricing page](https://www.quattr.com/pricing) is a demo form, and the [comparison page](https://www.quattr.com/compare/quattr-vs-profound) calls pricing custom.
- **It is a program, not a report.** The [homepage](https://www.quattr.com/) describes a Decide, Optimize, Create, Prove cadence with a strategist, connected Search Console and GA4 data, and prepared work that your team reviews before it ships. The value depends on who uses it.
- **A narrow publishing path.** The comparison page names WordPress as the native publishing integration "now" and other CMSs as coming soon. On another CMS, ask what the handoff looks like.
- **An uncertain trial.** Quattr's FAQ lists a demo, sandbox, free trial, proof of concept or paid pilot, depending on your use case.

Pick your reason, then the alternative: price clarity points to the public-price tools below, effort points to a snapshot or a lighter tracker, and the CMS question needs a straight answer from Quattr.

sections.heading: Which alternatives fit which need?
sections.body:
Match the alternative to your reason for leaving: a snapshot (AEOeye), daily tracking at a public price (Otterly, Peec AI, Nightwatch), credits with actions (AthenaHQ), or an enterprise quote (Profound). Each price below comes from the vendor's pricing page on 3 October 2026.

- **AEOeye.** A free audit asks ChatGPT three unbranded buyer questions and shows the full answers. The [$29 report](/) is paid once and adds Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity across ten questions. No history, no daily runs, no publishing. Best for: a first answer before you spend.
- **Otterly.AI.** [Lite is $29 a month](https://otterly.ai/pricing) for 15 prompts on ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity and Copilot, tracked daily; Claude, Gemini and AI Mode are paid add-ons. Standard is $189 for 100 prompts. Best for: the cheapest daily tracker.
- **Peec AI.** [Starter is $95 a month](https://peec.ai/pricing) for 50 prompts on three models you choose, tracked daily; Pro is $245 and Advanced $495. Best for: marketing teams that want a clean tracker with room to grow.
- **Nightwatch.** [Starter is €99 a month](https://nightwatch.io/pricing) (€79 billed yearly) for 50 AI prompts and 500 keywords, covering ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, AI Mode and AI Overview, with a 14-day trial and no card. Best for: rank tracking and AI tracking in one tool.
- **AthenaHQ.** A [free plan](https://athenahq.ai/pricing) gives 300 credits; Starter is $295 a month for 3,600 credits, where one credit is one AI response. Starter lists 11 models and on-page and off-page actions. Best for: teams that want actions, not just charts.
- **Profound.** Its [pricing page](https://www.tryprofound.com/pricing) offers a free 7-day trial (50 prompts daily on ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Overviews) and a custom Enterprise plan tracking up to nine engines. Best for: large teams that accept a sales process.

Our order for a buyer who is unsure: run the free audit to confirm the gap, then take the cheapest tracker that covers the engines your buyers use, and book a sales call only when the bottleneck is execution volume. Tracking beats a one-off report when you will act on trends, because [SparkToro's research](https://sparktoro.com/blog/new-research-ais-are-highly-inconsistent-when-recommending-brands-or-products-marketers-should-take-care-when-tracking-ai-visibility/) found ChatGPT and Google's AI almost never repeat the same brand list, so a single run is thin evidence.

![A signpost listing city names and directions with office buildings in the background](https://images.pexels.com/photos/11209154/pexels-photo-11209154.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

sections.heading: What dashboards does Quattr have, and what replaces them?
sections.body:
Quattr describes analyses and reports inside its platform, an embedded enterprise edition of Looker for custom dashboards, and a read-only MCP connection that lets an AI assistant query your data. Its comparison page lists the Looker dashboards as a feature, but Quattr has no published plans, so what is included for you is a sales question.

Public-price tools put dashboards behind higher tiers too:

- **Otterly** lists a Looker Studio connector from Standard ($189 a month).
- **Peec AI** lists Looker Studio integration on Advanced ($495 a month).
- **AthenaHQ** lists an executive dashboard with BI tool support, including Tableau, Power BI and Looker, on Enterprise.

If you only need charts for a weekly report, any tracker's built-in views will do. Pay for the connector only when someone needs the data inside another tool.

sections.heading: What does Quattr cost, for reference?
sections.body:
Quattr publishes no price. As of 3 October 2026 its pricing page asks for a demo and its comparison page says pricing is custom, so treat it as a quote-based purchase and use the public prices above as yardsticks only.

One trap is worth knowing. On that comparison page, "Starts at $99/month for SMBs" sits in the Profound column, as Quattr's claim about a competitor. Profound's own pricing page now shows only a free trial and a custom Enterprise plan for brands, so it is not an entry price for either vendor.

Our [Quattr cost guide](/answers/how-much-does-quattr-cost) lists what each source shows and five questions to ask before you book.

sections.heading: When is Quattr still the right choice?
sections.body:
Quattr is still the right choice when you already know AI visibility matters, someone owns SEO, and the bottleneck is producing and linking pages rather than measuring them. In that case an alternative that only reports will leave the real work undone.

- **Many pages to refresh or link.** Its GIGA agent and Internal Linking AI are built for that volume.
- **One vendor and a strategist.** Quattr bundles tracking, execution and a strategist, and says it replaces several tools. That is its claim, which we have not tested.
- **Your data already lives in Search Console and GA4.** The comparison page lists joins to both, so citations can be tied to sessions.
- **A WordPress site.** It is the CMS integration Quattr names.

If that is not you, start cheaper. In [AEOeye's crawler access study](/resources/ai-crawler-access-study-2026-10.csv) (3 October 2026), none of the seven sites compared here, Quattr's included, blocked an AI crawler in robots.txt (Otterly's returned an error, so we saw no rules). Only AEOeye and AthenaHQ served an llms.txt, and Otterly's returned a 403 so we could not tell. We think the file is [overrated as a lever](/blog/llms-txt-is-overrated), and a vendor's website tells you little about its product. Run the [free audit](/), then see [the full vendor field](/blog/best-ai-visibility-tools) or [AEOeye against Quattr](/vs/quattr).

keyTakeaways: Quattr publishes no price, is built for teams that run a program, and its trial route depends on your use case.
Public-price alternatives checked 3 October 2026: Otterly from $29 a month, Peec AI from $95, Nightwatch from €99, AthenaHQ free or $295, Profound a 7-day trial then Enterprise.
AEOeye is a one-off snapshot, not a tracker: free ChatGPT check, then $29 once for five engines.
Quattr remains the right call for a large site with an SEO owner and a need for prepared fixes.

faqs.q: What is the best free alternative to Quattr?
faqs.a: It depends what you want free. AEOeye's audit is free and asks ChatGPT three buyer questions. AthenaHQ has a free plan with 300 credits, Profound offers a free 7-day trial, and Nightwatch gives a 14-day trial without a card. Free options show you whether you are named; none replaces Quattr's prepared page fixes.

For ongoing tracking, Otterly's Lite plan is the cheapest listed at $29 a month for 15 prompts, as of 3 October 2026. For a single check, AEOeye costs $29 once for ten questions across five engines. Those are different jobs: a tracker repeats daily, a one-off report does not.

faqs.q: Which alternative is closest to Quattr?
faqs.a: None is identical. Quattr combines tracking, prepared page changes and a strategist. AthenaHQ's Starter plan lists actions and a content optimization agent, and Profound sells through a sales process like Quattr. Otterly, Peec AI and Nightwatch are trackers first. We have not tested any of them, so compare against your own page list.

faqs.q: Is AEOeye a full replacement for Quattr?
faqs.a: No. AEOeye is a one-time audit: three questions on ChatGPT free, ten questions on five engines for $29. It has no history, daily tracking or publishing. It replaces Quattr only if what you need is a first answer on whether AI names you.

On its own pages, Quattr tracks AI answers daily, joins them to Search Console and GA4 data, prepares page refreshes, new pages and internal links for your review, and assigns a strategist. It suits a team with an SEO owner and a large site. Those are Quattr's claims; we have not tested them.
